title: Retention scenarios & redaction controls overview — Crofter Analytics
next_steps: Send retention toggle quickstart and sample API calls
Share SOC2 + network architecture (private plane) doc
Schedule 1-week POC kickoff with Crofter infra team
action_items: Alicia Park: Email POC checklist and pricing worksheet — due 2029-02-09
Marcelo Ruiz: Prep an on-prem latency micro-benchmark plan and sample configs — due 2029-02-14
Daniel Cho (Crofter): Provide list of internal compliance reviewers and expected timeline — due 2029-02-12
summary: Redwood demo focusing on request storage toggles, PII redaction, and logging controls. Customer concerned about telemetry retention, regulatory auditability, and tradeoffs between hosted vs private. Agreed to a short POC to validate on-prem latency and retention policy enforcement.
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Alicia from Redwood Inference, AE on the Crofter account. Marcelo is our systems SE. Could we do quick intros?
[00:12] Nina Patel: Hi, Nina here, I run the data platform at Crofter.
[00:16] Daniel Cho: Daniel, security eng, I'll be validating the controls.
[00:19] Priya Menon: Priya, product, mainly interested in how toggles map to user controls.
[00:24] Marcelo Ruiz: Great to meet you all. Quick agenda — show the Console toggles for request storage, demo redaction pipeline, and then go over a POC plan.
[00:34] Alicia Park: Cool, and just to set expectations, we'll cover hosted defaults and the private deployment options — VPC or on-prem — and discuss where telemetry lives and how you can prune it.
[00:44] Nina: Perfect. Our main constraint is that we cannot keep any raw request text beyond 30 days in our analytics pipeline; anything PII must be redacted before landing in any logs. Also we want audit logs for model inference for compliance.
[00:58] Daniel: Yes and we need KMS-backed encryption for stored artifacts, and SSO for admin access.
[01:05] Marcelo: Makes sense. I'll start by sharing my screen to show the Console — bear with me while the screen share catches up.
[01:20] [screen share starts]
[01:23] Marcelo: This is the Redwood Console. At the top-level you'll see Request Storage (on/off), Retention window, and Redaction rules. The default hosted config keeps 7 days of telemetry but stores only vector embeddings and metadata if you enable "storeless mode."
[01:38] Priya: Storeless mode? Can you explain that a bit?
[01:41] Marcelo: Sure — storeless mode keeps ephemeral inference data only for the lifetime of the request; we still surface aggregated metrics to the Console, like token counts and error rates, but no request text or embeddings are persisted. It's a good fit for teams with strict PII policies. The UI lets you flip between full, truncated, and storeless modes per-route.
[01:58] Nina: Does truncated mode keep partial text or a hashed version?
[02:02] Marcelo: Truncated keeps a prefix up to X tokens (configurable) then drops the rest; hashed mode will store a SHA of the request to allow dedup checks without retaining content. The redaction engine runs before any persistence step.
[02:15] Daniel: How deterministic is redaction? We need to ensure names, SSNs, emails are caught; also avoid false positives for business-specific tokens.
[02:24] Marcelo: We have a layered approach — first a rules engine (regexes, dictionaries), then a model-based PII extractor that runs locally in the inference path, and finally a post-process sanitizer. You can add custom patterns per-tenant. There can be occasional misses in model detection — that's where the rules help.
[02:41] Alicia Park: Note that the Console exposes an eval playground for your dataset to run a quick scan against our default patterns — we'll share sample configs.
[02:50] Priya: Is the PII extractor part of the hosted pipeline only or can it run in private on-prem?
[02:55] Marcelo: It can run in both. For Redwood Private we ship the sanitizer as a containerized service that binds inside your VPC and uses your KMS. That way raw requests never leave your network.
[03:07] Nina: That's critical. We have a compliance requirement that certain PII never leaves our VPC.
[03:12] Marcelo: Understood. In private mode you get a private control plane and the option to disable any telemetric egress. The audit logs can be exported to your S3/GCS with encryption via your KMS or an HSM.
[03:24] Daniel: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) for embeddings and telemetry exports?
[03:28] Marcelo: Yes, CMKs via KMS integrations. We also support HSM-backed signing for audit trails if you need FIPS validations.
[03:36] Nina: About retention: can we set different windows per route? For example, payments routes 0 days, product QA 14 days.
[03:44] Marcelo: Yes, retention is route-scoped. The Console UI shows a policy matrix; you can also set defaults and apply overrides. There's an API to manage it if you want policy-as-code.
[03:54] Priya: What's the latency impact for redaction and storeless mode? We care about sub-200ms p95 for interactive features.
[04:02] Marcelo: Great question. For hosted with small models, redaction adds a small tail — typically 10–30ms if rules-only, and 40–80ms if the model extractor is invoked. For heavy model-based redaction or more complex regexes, it can be 100–150ms. In storeless mode there's less IO overhead, so sometimes it's actually faster since we skip persistence.
[04:24] Alicia: We'll share our latency profile table by deployment mode. The tradeoff usually is model-based redaction vs strict regex to guarantee zero leakage — regex is faster but brittle.
[04:35] Nina: We're thinking hybrid: inline regex for SSN/email, model extractors for unstructured NER. Can Redwood's Optimize suggest patterns?
[04:44] Marcelo: Yes, Redwood Optimize has a suggestion engine that looks at your traffic distribution and offers recommended tokenization and candidate redaction patterns, and can generate a default ruleset which you can review. In Private it runs locally; in hosted it's run in our opt cluster but never stores raw text if you enable storeless.
[04:59] Daniel: Regarding audit logs — we need immutable logs of admin actions and model version rollouts for compliance reviews.
[05:06] Marcelo: Audit trails include admin actions, API key rotations, model rollout events, and policy changes. They are write-once in the control plane and can be shipped to your archive bucket with object lock if you want immutability.
[05:18] [06:00] Nina: (chuckles) sorry jumped the timestamp — can you show a sample event?
[05:24] Marcelo: Sure, here's an example entry — note the fields: timestamp, actor, action, route, old_policy, new_policy, and a redaction flag showing whether raw request was truncated.
[05:35] Priya: How easy is it to run a retroactive scrub for a compliance takedown? Suppose a user requests deletion of all their interactions.
[05:43] Marcelo: We expose an API for subject access requests: give us identifiers (user id, hashed email, or request id), and the system will locate artifacts across storage backends and redact/purge them. For storeless mode there will often be nothing to delete. For embeddings or logs we support selective ejection and re-ingestion of scrubbed vectors.
[06:03] Daniel: And these deletion operations produce an audit entry, correct?
[06:07] Marcelo: Correct — every deletion or ejection creates an immutable audit record with actor and request id.
[06:12] Nina: Are there limits on the number of rules or throughput for the redaction engine? We do 10k reqs/sec at peak for some routes.
[06:20] Marcelo: For high throughput we recommend pushing simple regex rules inline and offloading the model-based checks to a secondary async pass for tagging. We have batching and KV-cache friendly paths to avoid per-token recompute. In Dedicated deployments you can scale redaction workers to match throughput.
[06:36] Priya: Can you show the API call to toggle route-level storage?
[06:40] Marcelo: Yes — (shows REST snippet) POST /v1/routes/{id}/policy { "store_mode": "truncated", "retention_days": 14, "redaction_profile": "payments-default" } — you can also patch the policy via SDK.
[06:55] Alicia: I'll paste that snippet after the call.
[06:58] Nina: About model variants — if you fall back from large to small model (for cost), does any change in logging happen? We want consistent retention regardless of model variant.
[07:08] Marcelo: Policies are orthogonal to model variant. The routing layer will preserve the route's policy, so logs and retention behave the same even if we route to a quantized variant for cost.
[07:18] Daniel: Is there a telemetry sampling option? For analytics we only need 10% of raw queries.
[07:24] Marcelo: Yes, sampling policies are configurable — you can sample by deterministic hashing, probabilistic sampling, or conditional sampling (e.g., sample only errors or long-running requests). Sampled data can be stored in a separate bucket and tagged appropriately.
[07:36] Priya: I saw earlier notes about hashed storage for dedupe — can that be reversible? We must ensure the SHA isn't reversible for PII.
[07:44] Marcelo: We use salted hashes with customer-provided salt option in Private mode. We document best practices; you can also use HMAC with your CMK so it's not reversible.
[07:55] Nina: What about developer debugging — our SREs need request payloads sometimes to triage. Is there a safe way to allow that?
[08:02] Marcelo: We support ephemeral developer access windows: time-bound unredacted playback that only works if an admin grants `debug.view` for a specific request id; the access is audited and can be toggled off. Also you can configure that only certain roles see raw content, enforced with SSO and RBAC.
[08:18] Daniel: On network isolation: If we go Dedicated versus Private, what's the difference?
[08:23] Marcelo: Dedicated means reserved GPU capacity in our managed cloud region but still goes through Redwood control plane; data can be configured to not persist outside your region. Private is the option where the control plane sits in your VPC or on-premises and you control all egress. For strict compliance you likely want Private.
[08:38] Nina: Time to procurement — we need pricing for a 3 month POC and monthly estimate for enterprise volumes.
[08:45] Alicia: We'll send a pricing worksheet. For POC we can give a capped credit and include limited dedicated capacity if you want to test high throughput.
[08:55] Priya: Can we run an on-prem micro-benchmark? Our main worry is tail latency when redaction runs model-based.
[09:01] Marcelo: Yes, that's in the POC scope — we'll provide a small harness you deploy; it will run sample traces and give p50/p95/p99 for both storeless and persisted modes.
[09:12] Nina: Good. Slight tangent — do you integrate with our SIEM for alerting on suspicious requests?
[09:17] Marcelo: Yes, you can forward alerts and audit events to your SIEM over syslog or SNS and we map events to common schemas.
[09:25] Daniel: One more: retention policies need to be visible in our config repo. Is there a terraform provider or API?
[09:31] Marcelo: We have a terraformer module in beta, but there is a stable REST/GraphQL API you can call from your CI to apply policies. We'll share the docs link after the call.
[09:41] Priya: Thanks. Any known gotchas?
[09:44] Marcelo: Two to call out — first, complex regexes can accidentally over-redact (we saw a case where product numbers were removed). Second, model-based redactors must be validated against your corp vocab to avoid misses. That's why we recommend hybrid rules + model.
[09:59] Nina: What about retention for embeddings — if we remove request text, do embeddings still leak PII?
[10:06] Marcelo: Embeddings can encode information; we offer an embedding-scrub transform (vector ejection + re-embedding on scrubbed text) or you can opt to never persist embeddings for sensitive routes. In some workflows we hash metadata and keep only token counts.
[10:19] Daniel: Let's talk timeline: if we start POC next week, how long should we expect for a basic integration?
[10:25] Alicia: Typical POC is 2–4 weeks: week 1 intake and infra, week 2 benchmark runs and policy tuning, week 3 validation and report. We can compress if you provide infra access early.
[10:36] Priya: Who from Redwood will be our day-to-day SE?
[10:39] Alicia: Marcelo will be the technical lead, I'm your AE for commercial. We'll also pull an infra engineer if we do private/on-prem.
[10:47] Daniel: Okay, cost concern — model variants and redaction will add to cost; can we set a hard cap?
[10:53] Alicia: Yes, you can set per-route spend caps and rate limits; the Console alerts when you're close and can auto-fallback to cheaper model variants or throttle.
[11:05] Marcelo: Also Optimize can suggest quantized variants and batching parameters that reduce per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs.
[11:13] Nina: Example — if we need sub-200ms p95 and 10k rps, what's the typical architecture?
[11:19] Marcelo: You'd likely use Dedicated pools for those high-throughput routes with persistent KV cache in front to reduce context recompute, and inline simple regex redaction. For occasional heavy redaction, route to async annotators.
[11:33] Priya: Can we demo the PII scan on a synthetic sample now?
[11:36] Marcelo: Sure, I'll open the eval playground — I'll paste a sample transcript with names and SSNs and run the default profile.
[11:48] [runs scan, pause]
[11:52] Marcelo: Results — it flagged three SSNs and two email addresses. It also suggested adding a corporate product ID pattern that it didn't catch. You can accept suggestions into a tenant ruleset.
[12:05] Nina: There are a couple of false positives on product codes, but looks fine. Good to be able to tune.
[12:12] Alicia: We're about halfway — want to go quickly over POC plan and acceptance criteria?
[12:18] Nina: Yes please.
[12:20] Marcelo: POC scope: (1) deploy sanitizer in your VPC, (2) run micro-benchmarks for two routes (payments, chat), (3) validate deletion and audit workflows, (4) verify SSO/SAML and CMK integration. Success criteria: p95 < 200ms for chat route with redaction rules, zero raw PII residing beyond configured windows, and reproducible deletion operations within 24 hours.
[12:45] Priya: Sounds good. For deletion reproducibility we need a test harness that demonstrates end-to-end.
[12:50] Marcelo: We'll include that harness.
[12:52] Daniel: Could you also include a compliance package with the network diagram and data flow mapping?
[12:56] Alicia: Yes, we'll attach a redwood-private-architecture.pdf and the SOC2/ISO attestations.
[13:03] Nina: Final question — can we lock retention policy at org-level so product teams can't accidentally change it?
[13:09] Marcelo: Yes — RBAC can lock route policies; only Owners or a specific role can change retention. The UI will show a lock icon and any attempted changes require a two-person approval for production routes.
[13:22] Priya: Great.
[13:24] Alicia: Quick recap of next steps: we'll send the pricing worksheet, POC checklist, sample API snippets, and the micro-benchmark harness. Marcelo will draft the benchmark plan. Crofter will share contact list for compliance reviewers.
[13:41] Nina: We'll aim to have the infra folks available Thursday for kickoff.
[13:45] Alicia: I'll follow up with calendar invite and attach the docs. Any other questions?
[13:50] Daniel: None from me.
[13:52] Priya: All good.
[13:55] Alicia: Thanks everyone — we'll close here.
[13:59] [meeting ends]
